meta.title: "Why don't you like reading?" — how a question makes your child agree before they even answer | Sila Slova
meta.description: Teach your child to spot the hidden assumption in a question and check it before agreeing. Game-based course for children aged 8–12.

hero.headline: "Why don't you like reading?" — and your child has already started explaining why?
hero.subheadline: The answer is already built into the question. By answering, your child agrees to something that may not even be true. They were made to agree before they answered.

media.alt: A child starting to defend themselves without noticing the assumption in the question

pain.title: A question that already contains the answer
pain.body:
"Why don't you like reading?", "when will you stop being late?", "why did you do it again?" — at school, at home, in everyday conversation. Your child starts answering — and doesn't even notice they've already agreed to something that may not be true.

This isn't just a question — it's a question with a hidden assumption. Before answering, the child already accepts the condition built inside it: that they "don't like reading", that they "are late", that they did it "again". And the conversation carries on as if it were true.

Without the skill to spot it, the child agrees automatically. The result — they accept someone else's version of reality without ever checking it. Not because they don't think, but because they don't see that the question already contains a claim.

faq.q: Is it a game or a learning course?
faq.a: Both at the same time. "Sila Slova" looks like a detective series, but every episode contains a hidden critical thinking lesson.

faq.q: What age is it suitable for?
faq.a: Ideal for 8–12 year olds. At this age, children are most receptive to new thinking patterns and haven't yet formed rigid biases.

faq.q: How much time is needed each day?
faq.a: 15–20 minutes per episode. Flexible schedule — your child can come back at any convenient time.

faq.q: Is registration required for the demo?
faq.a: No. The demo episode is fully open — no registration, no subscription, no personal data required.
